newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt concerned by 5p rise in price of a pint.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt concerned by 5p rise in price of a pint.

text.p: The Irish government said on Wednesday that it was concerned by news that the price of a pint of beer was set to go up by an extra five pence in Ireland.
Publicans are planning to raise the price paid for a pint although the government did not levy any extra taxation on beer in the the last three budgets, including the 1997 one unveiled last week.
Bruton said in a statement that he had held discussions with the Irish Competition Authority on Wednesday and they shared his concerns about possible anti-competitive features of the beer market.
"We are considering the next most effective response in the circumstances," he said.
Bruton said it was important that the industry be aware that the government had kept down excise duties to allow competitive pricing.
"It would not be in the interests of the industry to allow increases beyond
what is reasonable in a year after such restraint on the part of the government," Bruton said.
Earlier, commerce minister Pat Rabbitte said plans for the price rise, the second in less than two months, was "simply unacceptable in a low-inflation environment".
The latest proposed increase, topping up a similar one at the beginning of last month, will leave some Dublin drinkers paying as much as 2.25 Irish pounds for a pint of beer or stout.
